It is a kernel member under H1 `kernel_state` and is never exposed to owners.
126	
127	```gdscript
128	class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
129	var completed: bool
130	var epoch: int
131	var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
132		get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
133	func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
134	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
135	func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it
136	
137	class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
138	func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
139	func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))
140	
141	class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
142	var tick: int
143	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
144	func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
145	class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
146	class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
147	class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
148	                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
149	class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
150	                                                    # file: src/kernel/facets/notify_context.gd (ADR-0010 § 1.1, TD-01): a presenter handler must name it
151	```
152	
153	`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.
154	
155	**Placement of `NotifyContext`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-01)*: the subscriber, result and control-outcome handler context lives in `src/kernel/facets/` with `CompletionToken`, `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyEvent` and the other types a presenter must name (ADR-0010 § 1.1, ADR-0004 placement table), because a presenter's handler signature `(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` has to compile in `src/presentation/`. The tick-phase contexts (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`) stay in kernel core and are on ADR-0010's presentation deny list; there is no `*Context` glob.
156	
157	**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.
158	
159	**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. The kernel holds the call result as a `Variant` and tests identity with `is_same()`, so a coroutine state returned by an owner that hit `await` fails the check like any other non-token value. Anything else, including `null`, a type default, a coroutine state or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).
160	
161	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
162	
163	```gdscript
164	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
165	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
166	var phase: Phase
167	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
168	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
169	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
170	func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
171	func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
172	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
173	```
174	
175	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
176	
177	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
178	|---|---|---|
179	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
180	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
181	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
182	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
183	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
184	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |
185	
186	`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.
187	
188	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.
189	
190	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
191	
192	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
193	
194	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
195	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
196	
197	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.
198	
199	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
200	
201	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.
202	
203	### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants
204	
205	A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.
206	
207	**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)
208	
209	| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
210	|---|---|---|---|
211	| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
212	| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
213	| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
214	| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
215	| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
216	| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
217	| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
218	| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |
219	
220	**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**
221	
222	| Local | Name | Raised when |
223	|---|---|---|
224	| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
225	| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
226	| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
227	| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
228	| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
229	| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
230	| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
231	| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
232	| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
233	| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block, or a subscription to an unknown block (ADR-0004 § 2) |
234	| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
235	| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
236	| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
237	| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
238	| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
239	| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
240	| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |
241	
242	A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.
243	
244	**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning), and, added 2026-10-28 and classified as ADR-0004 §§ 2, 3, 5 and 7 define them, `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` (a subscribe-time refusal, including the `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule of check 6), `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID`, `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`, `EVENT_OVERFLOW` and `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` (dev, playtest and test builds only). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.
245	
246	Each owner's local code list is written with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward); its domain id is fixed now.
247	
248	### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet
249	
250	The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
251	
252	`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get_view(block_id: StringName) -> Object` (never `get`: a method named `get` overrides the native `Object.get()`, which is a load-time parse error on 4.7.2, probed, and ADR-0010's `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` rule), returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get_view` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get_view(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.
253	
254	A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
255	
256	### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule
257	
258	At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:
259	
260	1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
261	2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
262	3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
263	4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.
264	
265	**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.
266	
267	### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table
268	
269	States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).
270	
271	- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
272	- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
273	- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
274	- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
275	- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.
276	
277	The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.
278	
279	### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
280	
281	Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
282	
283	*(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07.)* The H1 **registries** group also holds, by name: `touch_serial` (a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written by every granted `open_for`; ADR-0004 § 7), the **hash-cache arrays** (`{hash, enc_len, serial}` as three parallel `PackedInt64Array`s sized once at the freeze; ADR-0005 §§ 5.1, 5.2), the per-block key-space table (ADR-0004 § 3) and the subscription tables (ADR-0004 § 2). **kernel_state** also holds the kernel-internal hash `SnapshotContext` of § 3 and the `kernel.clock` below. The H1 lint's fixed list is extended by exactly these names.
284	
285	**The `kernel.clock` view.** `kernel.clock` is an H1 member owned by this ADR. It carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` and is exposed to modules and the composition root only as a read-only view (getters `tick()`, `world_seed()`, `restore_epoch()`; no setters). `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary. **`world_seed`** is set before `INIT` (by `request_new_game`, or from the payload by `request_restore`) and does not change until the next new game or restore. **`restore_epoch`** is a `u32`, **read-only to owners, non-persisted and non-hashed**: it is in no state block, no canonical byte string, no `state_hash` and no snapshot header (ADR-0005 § 2.4). `request_restore` and `request_new_game` set it **before** the first `restore()` or `init_world`; Save/Load supplies the value and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006), but the kernel's copy is the only one the simulation can see. It is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0005 § 2.3); a lint forbids any other read in `src/sim/`.
286	
287	### Architecture Diagram
288	
289	```
290	BOOTING (ModuleFacet.registrar, one-way; nulled at the freeze)
291	  owner.setup(facet) ──► registrar.register_block(BlockDescriptor{... callables})
292	                         registrar.register_command(CommandTypeDescriptor)
293	                         registrar.register_hook(HookDescriptor)
294	                         registrar.register_key_space(KeySpaceDescriptor)       (ADR-0004 § 3)

371	### Implementation Guidelines
372	- **Must** register blocks, commands, hooks, fault domains and diagnostics channels only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register after the freeze.
373	- **Must** declare every kernel-invoked owner callable `-> CompletionToken` with `return ctx.complete()` as its **last** statement and nothing after `complete()` in that expression; **must never** declare one `-> void`, return a domain value, or use `assert()` or an engine error for control flow.
374	- **Must** report outcomes through `ctx` (`ok`/`reject`/`put`/`fault`); **must never** signal success or failure through the return value.
375	- **Must never** override a `CallContext` method in a subclass; subclasses only add methods.
376	- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(<its block>)` and mark dirty keys with `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator; **must never** rely on a property setter for dirty tracking, and **must never** write a block outside a scope.
377	- **Must** return a status from every Class A mutator (`OK`, `REFUSED`, or `-code`) and deliver data through a caller-owned `out` object; **must** stop and `return ctx.complete()` at the first non-`OK` status, with no second `ctx.fault`.
378	- **Must** make `restore` copy into the existing block object; **must never** replace the block object a facade wraps.
379	- **Must** keep block objects `RefCounted` and plain-data; **must never** make a block a `Resource` or `Node`, or hand out a live container from a view.
380	- **Must** declare fault codes pre-packed in the owner's `*_faults.gd` with its static `DOMAIN_ID`; **must never** reuse or renumber a code.
381	- **Must** declare `tolerates_stale` on every `after` edge between hooks that do not always coincide.
382	- **Must** keep every hook allocation-free in steady state; **must** call kernel callables with `Callable.call()` and a fixed argument list, **never** `callv` on the hot path.
383	- **Must** keep owners alive explicitly: a registered `Callable` does **not** own its object (Verification 3), so the composition root holds every owner in one strong-reference list from `BOOTING` to `SHUTTING_DOWN`; boot checks every registered callable `is_valid()` after the freeze.
384	- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable`, owners drop their facets and the composition root clears its owner list last; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value. The test starts from "callables do not own": an owner freed early shows up as an invalid callable at boot, not as a leak.
385	- **Must never** use `await` in a kernel-invoked owner callable or anything it calls (a lint over `src/sim/` and `src/kernel/`): a suspended call returns a coroutine state (caught as `INCOMPLETE`) but could later resume against a re-armed context and scope and write through them. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review.)*
386	- **Must never** let an owner callable subscribe to notifications (CR-10).
387	- **Must** put only duplicated packed arrays in a `snapshot` payload; **must never** return a live reference to a block's own array *(2026-10-28, TD-07)*.
388	- **Must** end every branch of an override of a typed-return owner callable in `return ctx.complete()` *(2026-10-28, TD-07)*.
389	- **Must** register a `KeySpaceDescriptor` with every block (ADR-0004 § 3) and emit P5 events only through `scope.emit_event`; **must never** read `restore_epoch` outside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` *(2026-10-28, TD-07)*.
390	- **Must** give a host service that owns no block only the `HostRegistrarFacet`; **must never** hand it a full `BlockRegistrar` *(2026-10-28, TD-07)*.
391	- **Build-mode equivalence** *(GDD command-simulation-layer, TR-cmd-053)*: a `STRICT_DEBUG` kernel and a `LENIENT_RELEASE` kernel fed the same command stream (one that raises no violation under `STRICT_DEBUG`) produce identical result records, identical final state and an identical `state_hash` over `ALL_SIM` (ADR-0005). The strict-only checks (the command round-trip copy of ADR-0002 § 9, the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, the `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` check in `RUNNING`) change only diagnostic counters and call `violation_handler`; they never alter a result, a write or a fault. A replay test runs one stream under both modes and compares result records and hash (TR-cmd-053).
392

15	## Summary
16	Over a hundred requirements from seventeen GDDs (the 65 rows of `tr-baseline.md`, the TR-saveload-028 to 042 gap rows and the cross-system rows the traceability matrix assigns here) need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a reserved PROFILE side file in the same container (built at the first PROFILE block, not at MVP), and a `restore_epoch` held in two alternating checksummed files that is made durable before every `request_restore`. The service is a tree-free `RefCounted` in `src/save/`; a thin `SaveHost` node in `src/game/` polls it once per frame and owns the window-close interception. Settings persistence is out of scope.

41	## Context
42	
43	### Problem Statement
44	The game's one failure consequence is death and restart from the last autosave (Pillar 5), and its horror depends on the player never being able to read the world through the save system (Pillars 1, 3, 4). That makes persistence unusually load-bearing: a bad write that costs a good generation destroys the campaign; a pause when the game saves tells the player a tell has closed; a restart that replays the identical threat draws makes death a free retry; a restart that lets quit choose the draws makes quit a reroll oracle; and a format that cannot be migrated strands every outside tester at the first schema change. The Save/Load GDD settles the behaviour and defers a dozen mechanism choices to "the atomic write, backup and thread model" ADR and to "the container ADR": what the bytes are, how a Windows rename is used safely, how a worker thread is owned, how a quit is waited for, how the 64-bit and JSON constraints are met, where `restore_epoch` lives and how it reaches the kernel, and whether the snapshot hitch is acceptable. Two probes (§ Engine Compatibility) also falsify two GDD sentences: `var_to_bytes` does encode objects, and `FileAccess.open` is not exclusive. Without one decision, each of the 14 persisted blocks would meet a slightly different container, and the first outside build would find the differences.
45	
46	### Constraints
47	- **Save/Load registers zero state blocks and zero hooks** (SL-17, TR-saveload-018): ring bookkeeping must live outside the world, or it rolls back with a restore.
48	- **Exactly one thread boundary** exists (architecture § Data Flow 7): the save writer. `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool`, `Mutex` and `Semaphore` are allowed only in `src/save/` (ADR-0010 IO-02), and `call_deferred`, `set_deferred`, `call_thread_safe` and `Engine.get_main_loop` are banned in `src/save/` as everywhere else in the foundation layers (SIM-12); this ADR cites those rules and does not restate them. The only cross-thread payload is a `PackedByteArray` (or `PackedInt64Array`) **handed over by ownership transfer (the sender keeps no alias) or as a `.duplicate()`, and never mutated by either side afterwards**; packed arrays are shared by reference in 4.7.2 (probe 16), plus pre-globalised absolute path strings, ints and a header template built for the job (TR-saveload-007; § 1.6 states the ownership rule, because the engine does not enforce one).
49	- **Capture is synchronous inside the kernel's `SAVING` state** at a tick boundary (TR-cmd-017, TR-saveload-009); `SAVING` is atomic within one boundary service and never spans a frame (ADR-0003 § 9, ADR-0001 § 1).
50	- **A bad file never produces `FAULTED`** (TR-saveload-014): the pre-check is a pure function of `(bytes, registry view, build constants)` and runs before the kernel is touched.
51	- **Block objects are `RefCounted`, restore copies into the existing object** (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2). No `Resource` or `.tres` path, ever (a script can ride in one).
52	- **Integer-only simulation** (ADR-0005); JSON parses numbers as `float` (probed), so no 64-bit or hashed value may travel as a JSON number (S-1).
53	- **No wall clock in any sim decision** (kernel H9; ADR-0010 SIM-02): every millisecond I/O timeout in this ADR (`WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`, `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS`) reads the injected `Clock` port (`src/kernel/ports/clock.gd`, `now_us()`; `FakeClock` in tests) and changes no sim state (SL-23). The one wall-time value, `created_unix` and the time `SaveInfo` displays, comes from the `WallClock` port (`src/save/wall_clock.gd`, `now_unix() -> int`; sole implementation `src/game/system_wall_clock.gd`, ADR-0010 TD-11), injected into `SaveService.setup()` only. It is display metadata and is **never** an ordering key (the generation number is the only order), a gate, a hash input or a sim input.
54	- **No autoload or static singleton** (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`): Save/Load is constructed and injected by the composition root.
55	- **Fault codes** follow ADR-0003 § 6: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, domain 1 = `save_load`, append-only.
56	- **Single player at MVP**; co-op replication, guest carry-over and Steam Auto-Cloud are later tiers and constrain only the path layout.
57	
58	### Requirements
59	- One container format for WORLD generations and the PROFILE store, self-verifying by a trailer that lives outside the header.
60	- A write that never overwrites in place, never deletes a generation before its successor verified, never blocks the main thread, and never starts while the kernel is `FAULTED`.
61	- A load that classifies every failure (corrupt, incompatible, owner-failed, not-reproduced) and decides the next action from the class.
62	- Two-level versioning with an obligation to migrate that begins at the first outside build, and development saves that are refused rather than half-migrated.
63	- `restore_epoch` that survives a process kill, a lost manifest and a step-back, is durable before the restore that uses it, and reaches the sim only as an argument.
64	- A quit that waits for its write by polling, with a timeout, and never hangs the process on a stuck worker; the window close button, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown take the same path (§ 1.6).
65	- A recorded ruling on the snapshot hitch (OQ-14) and a named spike for every engine claim the reference does not source.
66	
67	## Decision
68	
69	The decision has three parts, numbered so each can be reviewed on its own: **§ 1 the container and the write path**, **§ 2 versioning and migration**, **§ 3 the restore epoch**. Behaviour already fixed by the GDD (SL-1 to SL-25, T-3 to T-9, F-1 to F-10) is cited, not restated; this ADR decides what the GDD left as `[UNV]`, as an "ADR candidate", or wrong.

106	```
107	
108	### 1. The container and the write path
109	
110	**1.1 Layout.** The file layout is SL-1 as written: 8 bytes of magic, `u32` LE `header_len`, UTF-8 JSON header, concatenated block payloads, a 32-byte SHA-256 trailer over every preceding byte (the **format law**: for every layout, forever, the last 32 bytes of any file bearing the magic prefix hash `[0, size - 32)`). Choices this ADR adds:
111	
112	- **Magic.** `53 59 4E 53 45 41 1A` (`"SYNSEA"` and a SUB/EOF byte, so a text-mode tool stops early), then the container-layout id byte (`01` for `FORMAT_VERSION` 1). The file extension is `.sav`.
113	- **Streamed hashing, scoped.** Save/Load's own `HashingContext` (`HASH_SHA256`) use is limited to `payload_sha256`, the trailer and `registry_epoch`, fed in chunks (`update`) so no hash needs a second whole-file copy; **`update` is never called with a zero-length chunk** (it errors), so an empty payload or header is skipped. `state_hash` and every `block_state_hash` are computed by the **kernel, uncached, during the `SAVING` capture** (ADR-0005 §§ 4.7, 5.4) and arrive in the snapshot outcome; Save/Load never computes or re-derives an `H64`. Container byte layout (`encode_u32` for `header_len`, `slot_epoch` bytes) and integrity hashing in `src/save/` use the byte writers that ADR-0005 § 1.7 row 8 forbids in the kernel, sim and block owners; `src/save/` is exempt because that output never feeds `H64` or `state_hash` (TD-12). Reading a candidate checks `FileAccess.get_length()` against `MAX_SAVE_BYTES` first, then reads. Whole-file reads use `get_buffer` loops or `FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes`; both are acceptable, the length cap comes first.
114	- **One payload form.** Every block payload is `var_to_bytes(dictionary)` of the owner's plain-data snapshot **Dictionary**; that every persisted block `put`s a Dictionary is a Save/Load-side precondition checked by the type walk (the decoded root of each block must be a `Dictionary`), not a change to ADR-0003's `put(payload: Variant)` signature. **Canonical bytes are produced by the kernel (ADR-0005 § 3.1) and never stored:** the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays; storage is `var_to_bytes`; hash input is ADR-0005's TLV of the same payload. The GDD's second form ("the owner's own canonical byte form as raw bytes", SL-2) is **dropped as a container form**. Reason: one decode path, one type walk, and a restore hand-off that is always a `Dictionary`, matching ADR-0003's `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version, ctx)` (no `form` field and no byte-blob hand-off shape to invent). State equality is `state_hash`, never file bytes (probed: insertion order changes the bytes).
115	- **Header** is the closed list of SL-1 plus the additions of § 2 (`catalogue_version` is already there). The per-block hash field is named `block_state_hash` (SL-16) throughout, beside `enc_len`; the header `state_hash` is the kernel's `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` from the capture outcome. `seats` is an array of `PlayerId` ints (MVP `[1]`: single-player is host peer 1 → PlayerId 1, ADR-0002 § 3, kernel CR-7; corrected 2026-10-29 from `[0]`): non-empty, unique, in range, covering every PER_PLAYER key; no peer id, binding table or controlled-entity table is stored, and the kernel rebuilds bindings after a restore (TR-saveload-037). `created_unix` is written from the `WallClock` port and is display metadata only. Unknown extra keys are ignored when `min_reader_version` is satisfied; a missing required key refuses.
116	
117	**1.2 Interchange and the trust model (corrects SL-2).**
118	
119	1. **The encoder does not refuse objects (probed).** `var_to_bytes` silently encodes an `Object` as an `EncodedObjectAsID` and `bytes_to_var` returns it. SL-2's wording "the form that does not encode objects" is wrong in the direction that matters: a stray object in a `snapshot()` would reach disk. The defence is therefore **not** the encoder. It is (a) the type walk, which rejects `TYPE_OBJECT` explicitly (an `EncodedObjectAsID` is an Object), and (b) the write-side `VERIFYING` stage, which decodes and walks the bytes the worker just wrote (T-4), so an object-bearing snapshot is caught at write (`SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE`, previous generations intact) and never first at a death.
120	2. **Decode with `bytes_to_var` only.** `var_to_bytes_with_objects` and `bytes_to_var_with_objects` are forbidden outright, as are `Resource`, `.tres`, `.res` and `ResourceLoader` for any save path. `bytes_to_var` of hostile input returns `null` and logs an engine `ERROR` that code cannot suppress (probed): so the decode runs only **after** the trailer, the block table and `payload_sha256` have passed, and a `null` result for a block that must be a `Dictionary` is `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_DECODE_FAILED`. A forged file with correct hashes can still produce engine error lines; that is a tamper case, accepted, and the fuzz suite is told (Risks, ADR-0010 assumption).
121	3. **Allowed types, enforced by the walk, not the encoder (probed: `Vector2i` round-trips, so the ban is policy).** `null`, `bool`, `int` (full 64 bits, § 1.3), finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` with `String` or `int` keys, and the packed arrays `PackedByteArray`, `PackedInt32Array`, `PackedInt64Array`. Forbidden: `Vector2i` and every vector or rect, `Color`, `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath`, `StringName` as a key or a value (a `StringName` is decoded as one, probed, so it must be rejected, not coerced; ADR-0003's `StringName` block ids and the in-memory staged payload keys of § 3.6 are memory-only and never enter a file, where block ids are header `String`s), and non-finite floats. Typed `Array[T]` and `Dictionary[K, V]` **round-trip their values** through the encoder (probed; type preservation is not asserted), which settles SL-2's "untyped until the spike" note: snapshots may use typed or untyped containers; the walk checks the decoded element types either way. Bounds: `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH` 16, `MAX_DECODE_NODES` **provisional 100 000** (the GDD knob is 250 000; typical saves are 10 000 to 30 000 nodes and the bound stays lowered until the walk timing of SAVE-WRK-1 f is measured, then is raised only as far as that timing allows; a packed array counts as one node, unchanged), per `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` and `MAX_SAVE_BYTES`. Owners' `restore()` still validates meaning; the walk validates only type and size.
122	4. **JSON appears only in the header and in the dev-only `dump-save`.** A dump renders any `int` whose magnitude is at or above 2^53 as a lowercase decimal string and any `PackedByteArray` as `Marshalls.raw_to_base64`; it is diagnostics, never a load path (TR-lsg-022).
123	5. **No compression** in the MVP (`codec` 0; 1 reserved). A size alarm at `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB is diagnostics only.
124	6. **Roots and staging.** The decoded root of every block must be a `Dictionary`, and the in-memory staged payload of § 3.6 is built from those. `Dictionary.make_read_only()` on a staged payload is **shallow** (probe 14): it is a convenience, never a guarantee, and owners must still copy what they keep. A deep read-only snapshot, where an owner wants one, is built by the owner from `duplicate(true)` at capture.

150	- **Reaping and lifetime.** Each poll calls `wait_to_finish()` **only** on a job whose thread reports `not is_alive()` (probed: returns at once with the callable's value). A dead thread with no terminal `WRITTEN`/`FAILED` status is `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`: `save_status` `FAILED`, `fail_n` + 1, the ring position released, the `.tmp` left to T-6. **A live thread is never joined**: `Thread.wait_to_finish` and the pool wait take no timeout (training knowledge), so a join at the `DEAD` boundary could hang the frame on a hung write. **Every `WriteJob` stays referenced from `SaveService.jobs` until it is reaped or the process exits**, including an abandoned job: a `Thread` object freed while its thread still runs logs the same `~Thread` warning as the quit probe and detaches the worker from any owner, orphaning its buffers, so dropping a live job on abandonment or on `SaveService` teardown is forbidden and a freed live job is a fault in debug builds.
151	- **Abandonment** is SL-10 as written (`write_epoch` bump, position claimed, `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` 2, `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 000, `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` 5 000, all measured on the injected `Clock` port). A job that lands a generation after being abandoned is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`.
152	- **Quit during a write: "bounded join" is bounded polling.** Process exit does not wait on a busy worker (probed: an 8 s sleeping worker did not delay exit past 0.68 s; the engine prints a `~Thread` WARNING and an ObjectDB leak report, which are expected and are ADR-0010's to allow-list, § 8.6). Save & Quit therefore **polls** the `QUIT` job under `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` 3 000 on the injected `Clock` and calls `request_shutdown` on `WRITTEN`; on timeout it does not abandon (a late completion is simply a `QUIT` generation, SL-6), reports `FAILED`, and the Chart Table offers the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving". An abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the operating system and its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. A worker blocked in a syscall rather than a sleep, or one that touches freed singletons while the engine tears down at exit, is **UNVERIFIED** (SAVE-WRK-1 d tests a worker mid-`store_buffer` and mid-`rename` at quit, on dev and release builds; the `quit_requested` check between stages shortens the tail).
153	- **Window close and OS quit (TR-saveload-039: Partial here; the quit transition is ADR-0003's `SHUTTING_DOWN` state, entered only through ADR-0002's `request_shutdown`; ADR-0030 owns the UI).** The window X button, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown deliver `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` (and, on mobile, `NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST`), and `SceneTree` auto-accepts it by default and quits at once, which would cut a write in flight. `SaveHost` therefore sets `get_tree().auto_accept_quit = false` on entering the tree and forwards both notifications to `SaveService.on_close_request()`, which routes by kernel state as TR-saveload-039 lists: `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` write a `QUIT` generation then quit, `LOADING` defers, `SAVING` settles then dedupes or writes, `DOWNED`, `FAULTED` and boot screens write nothing, and a failed or timed-out write holds the close (the quit-without-fresh-save flow above). It **never blocks**: if a `QUIT` or `AUTO` write is in flight it polls under `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, then calls `ControlHandle.request_shutdown()`. **`request_shutdown` is the only place `get_tree().quit()` is reached.** A close request that arrives during the epoch wait of § 3.3 is held until `EPOCH_DURABLE` or the 2a path completes. A test drives the close-request path with an injected stalled worker.

What does work on Windows (probed): a file held open makes `rename_absolute` and `remove_absolute` of it fail with `ERR_FAILED`, for READ and WRITE handles alike. The lock is therefore: the process that opens a campaign keeps a `FileAccess` handle on `campaign.lock` open (write mode, containing its process id, diagnostic only) for the campaign's lifetime; a second process tests ownership by renaming the file to `campaign.lock.probe` and back; a failure means "held", and it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY** (SL-10, AC-SL-147). `DirAccess` reports a missing source and a held target with the same `ERR_FAILED` (probed), so the probe **runs only when `campaign.lock` exists**; a missing file means "not held": the process creates it and holds the handle. A READ handle held for the campaign's lifetime suffices (probed: READ-held targets also fail rename and remove), which avoids depending on WRITE-mode truncation. A crashed holder releases its handle with the process, so there is no stale-lock case and no process-id liveness check is needed (`OS.is_process_running` is probed true for the own id, but whether it answers for a foreign non-child process is **UNVERIFIED** and is not used). **Handle lifetime:** a GDScript `FileAccess` closes when its last reference goes away (scope exit, reassignment, `null`, freeing the owner), so the handle is a **member of `SaveService`** (never a local), is never reassigned or nulled until the campaign closes, and a debug assertion checks `FileAccess.is_open()` in each frame poll. **Accepted exposure:** when the lock is not held the probe moves the file aside for an instant, and a third process starting at that moment sees "missing = not held" and also acquires it; for a single-instance guard this is acceptable and recorded, not engineered around. On Linux and the Deck, rename of an open file is expected to succeed (**UNVERIFIED**, SAVE-WRK-1 g), so the lock gives no protection there; Steam launches a single instance by default. The whole mechanism is best effort and deferrable to Alpha (OQ-D); if deferred, `campaign.lock` is not created at MVP and AC-SL-147 moves with it.

157	**1.8 The PROFILE split (reserved at MVP).** SL-9 as written: one kernel snapshot, split by `persist_scope` at write time; WORLD blocks to the generation, PROFILE blocks to `profile.sav` (same container, `file_kind` `PROFILE`, no `state_hash`, no `restore_epoch`), same atomic procedure with a **ring of one plus a permanent `.bak`** (the swap keeps the `.bak` instead of deleting it). **Zero PROFILE blocks ship at MVP, so the PROFILE file mechanism (ring of one, `.bak`, change-detection trigger, `PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS` 300) is specified here but is built and tested with the first PROFILE block, not before Alpha;** `file_kind` and `persist_scope` stay reserved in the format so that nothing needs migrating later. An in-session restore passes **only WORLD blocks** to `request_restore`, so PROFILE blocks are never rolled back (TR-cmd-017, TR-saveload-019); a cold open loads each scope whole from its own file. When built, a profile write is triggered when the **uncached `block_state_hash`es the kernel returns in the snapshot outcome** (TD-05) differ from those recorded at the last PROFILE write (never ADR-0005's cached hashes, TD-24), on `QUIT`, and at most every `PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS`. `scope` (SHARED/PER_PLAYER) and `persist_scope` (WORLD/PROFILE) are orthogonal: `suit.state`, `sanity.state` and `sanity.ledger` are PER_PLAYER x WORLD and roll back with the death stub (TR-suit-029, TR-webmap-030). **Display settings are not PROFILE state** (host-local Chart Table state, CT-19); see the scope note in the Ordering Note.

159	**1.9 Capture cost and the snapshot hitch (OQ-14).** The kernel owns capture (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7, a ceiling, kernel GDD), including the **uncached** `state_hash` and per-block `block_state_hash`/`enc_len` computed in `SAVING` (ADR-0005 §§ 4.7, 5.4). The unmeasured share is the owners' real `snapshot()` implementations and the kernel's capture-time `H64` hash. A 32-block snapshot reaching 16.7 ms (TR-cmd-032) therefore exceeds the 14.9 ms desktop frame target for **one frame per autosave** and no more; the autosave gate already keeps that frame away from tells (SL-5). The synthetic half is measured by SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT f; the real-owner half by SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, which also decides which rung is needed. **Mitigation rungs, in order, only if the measurement shows the frame is visible (P99 above `16.7 - P99(baseline CPU frame work)`, the formula already in `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS`):** (1) **Deferred, off by default.** The kernel may skip `snapshot()` for a block whose ADR-0005 cache entry is valid by touch serial (`entry_valid`) since the last capture, reusing the previous encoded bytes. (3) Split capture across frames, which the kernel's atomic-`SAVING` rule forbids today and needs a kernel GDD amendment. Rungs 2 and 3 are not decided here. **Type-walk cost (engine review E10):** the load-side walk is a GDScript loop, plausibly 0.3 to 1 microsecond per node per check (**UNVERIFIED**), so a typical 10 000 to 30 000 node save costs about 5 to 20 ms and the old 250 000-node bound could cost 100 ms or more; the walk therefore runs on the hot-copy worker when it can, `MAX_DECODE_NODES` is provisionally 100 000 (§ 1.2), and SAVE-WRK-1 f carries the target "walk at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes". The death stub's single synchronous attempt (SL-11) is the case this protects.
160	
161	**1.10 Pre-check, recovery and failure classes.** T-5 (the 23-step ordered pre-check), T-6 (crash recovery) and the failure classes of SL-11 stand as written. This ADR adds three things:
162	
163	- **A newer catalogue is INCOMPATIBLE, not owner-failed.** After step 12 (`tick_rate`) and before step 13 (the block table): a header `catalogue_version` greater than the running build's is `SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER`, class INCOMPATIBLE, stop, no quarantine ("made by a newer build"). Without it, a downgrade would surface as `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` or `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, an *owner-reported* failure that quarantines a good file after `QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES` 2. A *lower or equal* version proceeds: owners resolve renamed defs through ADR-0007's alias path. `catalogue_hash` is diagnostic only and never gates a load.
164	- **The pre-check is a pure static function** `PreCheck.run(bytes: PackedByteArray, registry: RegistryView, build: BuildConstants) -> PreCheckResult`, no clock, no file handle, no `Node`, unit-tested over in-memory byte arrays (TR-saveload-014). `RegistryView` is a plain-data snapshot of `(block_id, supported_versions, persist_scope, persist, added_in_format)` triples that Save/Load builds once after the registry freeze; `RegistryView` and `BuildConstants` live in `src/save/` (built by Save/Load from the frozen registry and the build, no import edge to `data`).
165	- **Reproduction mismatch stays a diagnostic.** The kernel's K-4 verdict arrives in `ControlOutcome` (ADR-0002 § 6); `SL_VERIFY_NOT_REPRODUCED` is never a fallback reason (TR-saveload-015).
166	
167	**1.11 Fault domain 1 and the closed reason sets.** `src/save/save_load_faults.gd` (`class_name SaveLoadFaults extends RefCounted`, `const DOMAIN_ID: int = 1`, packed codes `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | n`, and `const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH", ...]` indexed by the local code with index 0 = `&""`, the shape of ADR-0003's `GraphFaults.NAMES`) holds the closed sets `SL_PRECHECK_*`, `SL_WRITE_*`, `SL_LOAD_*`, `SL_VERIFY_*`, `SL_EPOCH_*`, `SL_QUIT_*`, `SL_NEW_GAME_*` and `SL_BOOT_*`, and Save/Load calls `register_fault_domain(1, &"save_load", NAMES)` in `BOOTING` through the BOOTING-only registrar facet that ADR-0003 gives a host service (limited to `register_fault_domain`; no block or hook registration), so diagnostics print `save_load.PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH`. **None of these faults the kernel**: a bad file, a failed write and a refused quit are values and diagnostics, and the kernel's own codes (`CAPTURE_ERROR` 7, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` 6, `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` 4, `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` 5, all domain 0) are the unreachable backstops behind Save/Load's pre-check. Registering a domain is neither a block nor a hook, so TR-saveload-018 holds. Knob range and invariant failures (`SL_BOOT_KNOB_RANGE`, `SL_BOOT_KNOB_INVARIANT`) are **domain 2** content boot errors raised by the ADR-0007 `ScalarTable` machinery (TR-saveload-024 is ADR-0007's); only the cross-check of § 2.3, which needs the live registry, raises domain 1 `SL_BOOT_*`.
168	
169	**1.12 The host API and what Save/Load may observe.** SL-21 as written: `new_game(world_seed)`, `continue_campaign()`, `save_and_quit()`, `cancel_held_close()`, read-only `campaign_info()`, `list_saves()`, `retire_campaign`, `delete_campaign`, and the host-local reads `save_status`, `fail_escalated`, `SaveInfo`, `restore_reason`, `restore_epoch` (diagnostic), `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`. No `save_now`, no `load(generation)` outside dev builds, no command registered (TR-saveload-023). Save/Load is a **polling control-plane caller, not a subscriber** (SL-13; TD-09): it holds a `ControlHandle` and a `save_load` facet of read views, subscribes to nothing and gets no end-of-tick callback and no sixth subscriber class. `SaveService.poll_frame()` (called by `SaveHost`, § 1.6) compares **monotonic counters** with the last values it saw; counters are chosen over level flags or `last_*_T` so that several events inside one catch-up frame are not lost. **The observation set (Save/Load's decision, owned here):** `kernel.clock`, `controller.state.loco_state` and `carry_ref` and `suit` `carried_id` (the SL-5 gate rows; TR-suit-035), `suit` `vitals_state`, `graph` failures, `attention.view`, Assembly's `ragged_breach_open()` and `last_shape_change_T()`, Interaction's `last_salvage_T()`, and the **conditional `web.state` read-view members `pod_arrived_seq: int` and `berthed_seq: int`**, recorded as a requirement on the Web Map ADR (Save/Load's half of TR-webmap-023). Until the Web Map ADR supplies them, the POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED triggers are absent and never fire (GDD rule: an event whose owner read is absent never fires). The last-seen copies are host-local and are re-read after a load, so a load never fires an autosave. ADR-0004 OQ-3 is closed from this side: Save/Load polls owner read views, there is no subscription class. Save/Load never reads a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view and never writes a block. It registers one `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler` method `Callable` with the signature `(outcome: ControlOutcome, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` that returns a token on every path, and uses it for the snapshot outcome (payload plus the hash data of § 1.1) and the K-4 verdict; `request_snapshot()` itself returns `void`.
170	
171	### 2. Versioning and migration
172	
173	**2.1 Two levels, as SL-14.** `format_version` (container) is migrated by Save/Load; `schema_version` (per block) is migrated only by the owner inside `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` as a chain of registered pure functions `(old Dictionary) -> new Dictionary`. Save/Load never rewrites block data. `min_reader_version` equals `format_version` on every write in the MVP. A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade-then-upgrade cannot half-migrate a file.
174	
175	**2.2 The block contract in ADR-0003 terms.** Reconciling SL-15 with the registered owner-callable contract (ADR-0003 § 1, registry `owner_callable_contract`): a persisted block registers `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state` and `post_restore` as `Callable`s each returning `ctx.complete()`, with `supported_versions`, `persist_scope` and `restore_after` in its `BlockDescriptor`.
176	
177	- `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload: Dictionary)`: a deep copy (no aliasing of live state, so the encode may later leave the main thread; packed arrays in the payload are duplicates, never live references, ADR-0003 snapshot contract), plain data per § 1.2, rows sorted by id, no derived caches, no object references, transient fields normalised (TR-pc-020).
178	- `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx)` is **two-phase: decode and validate into scratch, then copy the contents into the existing block object**. This is the single wording of the rule; "whole-block replace" and "swaps whole tables from scratch" in owner GDDs mean *replace the block's contents*, never the object (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2: read-view facades are long-lived).
179	- **Failure is reported through `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`** with the owner's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping; the kernel fires `load_failed` and Save/Load maps it to the `RESTORE_FAILED` class of SL-11. Owner GDDs that describe `(ok, reason, detail)` mean this (ADR-0003 sync, not this ADR's to change).
180	- `post_restore(ctx)` rebuilds derived caches and cross-block verification; `default_state(ctx)` fills a block missing from an older file whose `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`.
181	- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.
182	
183	**2.3 Block versions are data, cross-checked at boot.** `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one committed file `assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json` (loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline in the composition root as a closed-schema table and injected, with the Save/Load `ScalarTable`, into `SaveService.setup()` as plain data, so `save` needs no import edge to `data`; `save` may type variables with ADR-0007's published value types, TD-27), not in `BlockDescriptor`, so ADR-0003's descriptor field list is unchanged. After the registry freeze, the composition root runs `SaveBootCheck.verify(block_versions, registry_view)`: a mandatory-derivation mismatch, a registered block that is also retired (`SL_BOOT_RETIRED_BUT_REGISTERED`), or a missing entry fails boot with a domain-1 `SL_BOOT_*` code and the root never starts the kernel. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory iff its `added_in_format` is at most the file's `format_version`**; the MVP set in SL-25 is the *result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list.
184	
185	**2.4 `registry_epoch` and `catalogue_version`.** `registry_epoch` (the header field that tells "the registry moved" from corruption) is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text of the sorted lines `block_id:schema_version:added_in_format\n` for every persisted block, as lowercase hex. It uses `HashingContext` directly, **not** H64 or the canonical encoding, so it depends on neither ADR-0005 nor the kernel. A file whose `registry_epoch` differs from the running build's and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev: never CORRUPT, never quarantined (SL-11, T-5 steps 18 and 21). `catalogue_version` is the Item DB's single integer offered by ADR-0007 § 3.4; it is written in the header as an `int`, and its only gating use is the newer-than-build refusal of § 1.10.
186	
187	**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written (they are `hash_algo` ids, not hash values: no `H64` value is reserved as a sentinel, ADR-0005). An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.
188	
189	**2.6 Policy and fixtures (SL-14, unchanged).** The migration machinery exists from format 1. Two goldens: `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/` (regenerated freely until the registry settles) and `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/` (generated from the real registry at the first outside build, immutable, with a CI schema-drift fingerprint: the `registry_epoch` of the committed shapes may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump). The obligation to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project; before it, a mismatched development save is refused as "made by an incompatible development build". This is the same moment ADR-0007's id ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`; one project-level decision flips both.
190	
191	### 3. The restore epoch
192	
193	**3.1 Ownership and storage.** Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`, an unsigned 32-bit integer (an `int` in `[0, 2^32 - 1]`) starting at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18); it has exactly one owner and registry entry. It lives in a per-slot **pair of side files**, `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin` and `slot_epoch_b.bin`, each **12 bytes: the epoch as `u32` LE, a sequence number `seq` as `u32` LE, then the CRC32 of those 8 bytes as `u32` LE** (the GDD / TR-saveload-020 format of `u32` plus CRC32 gains the `seq` field; GDD sync). The reader takes the valid file (size 12, CRC matches) with the higher `seq`; the writer always overwrites the **older** file in place (an invalid file, or the lower `seq`) with `seq = max + 1`, flushes, closes, re-reads and checks the CRC (that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report). **No rename and no remove is involved**, so there is never an instant with no valid epoch file: a kill mid-write corrupts only the file being written and the other still holds the previous durable value. (A single file replaced by rename-over would, on Windows, probably be remove-then-rename, § 1.5, open a window in which the file is absent, and let the rebuild rule of § 3.4 yield `max(header copy) + 1`, which can be lower than an epoch already advanced, for example after two deaths with no autosave between them, replaying one set of threat draws; engine review E2.) `seq` saturates at 2^32 - 1, unreachable in practice because the epoch saturates first. `SlotEpoch.encode` calls `resize(12)` before any `encode_u32` (probe 17). **CRC32 is hand-rolled** (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, init and final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`, bitwise, over 8 bytes): `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32` (probed), the scripted loop matched the standard check vector, its cost is of order microseconds, and a truncated hash was rejected as a gratuitous change to the GDD format. The vector `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test. The files are in no generation, so no generation's bytes, trailer, `state_hash` or any key derived from them changes after `VERIFYING`; this is what makes SL-12's REBASED baseline key stable (R14). Each WORLD generation's header carries a **read-only write-time copy** (`restore_epoch`, an int below 2^32) used only by the rebuild rule of § 3.4; it is never rewritten.
194	
195	**3.2 When it advances (R13, unchanged).** A death-stub restore and a `FAULT_RECOVERY` always advance it. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`) advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation: that Continue **carries the epoch unchanged and writes nothing**, so Save & Quit then Continue replays the threat draws an uninterrupted run would meet and quit buys nothing. An advance is `restore_epoch := min(2^32 - 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, saturating and logging at the top; a step-back, a demotion, a quarantine or a lost manifest cannot lower it. A stub that finds nothing loadable restores nothing and does not advance it. The Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read the epoch.
196	
197	**3.3 Durable before the restore is requested (R14, with the polling decided).** After selection, pre-check and staging, Save/Load computes the new value and hands the `slot_epoch` write (the older of the two files, § 3.1) to the worker **as its own job**, never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job, and polls it once per frame from `poll_frame` (never blocking, never joined). Only on `EPOCH_DURABLE` does it call `ControlHandle.request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`, so the kernel's `LOADING` holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service. On the death stub the kernel is `RUNNING` from the `DEAD` boundary to that call (at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` 500 on the injected `Clock`, 30 frames); the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed, and a `restore_pending` latch refuses **Save/Load's own capture requests** and answers a further restore trigger with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`. **Save/Load cannot refuse a pause:** pause requests come from PauseGate's own `ControlHandle` (ADR-0002). If the player pauses during the wait, the restore would be requested from `PAUSED`; this ADR therefore requires that either PauseGate or the Chart Table suppresses pause while a seat is `DEAD` (ADR-0030), or that ADR-0003's transition table lists `request_restore` from `PAUSED` as well as `RUNNING` (OQ-J, owed by ADR-0003 or ADR-0030). A test pauses during the epoch wait and asserts the restore still reaches `LOADING` exactly once. The Player Controller's DEAD hand-off (TR-pc-022) is honoured only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`.
198	
199	**3.4 Failure and recovery.**
200	- **Write fails or times out (2a):** Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, sets `save_status` `FAILED`, and the worker retries the file with the next write job and after every later `WRITTEN` generation while memory is ahead of disk. A kill before then may replay that epoch once (OQ-25, an accepted and listed exposure: the device is failing and no write can fix that).
201	- **Both epoch files missing or invalid (2b):** (one valid file is a normal read, not a failure) the value reads as `max(newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, and is rewritten by the worker into the older slot. Deleting the side files by hand therefore re-keys the next stretch once, a tampering exposure of the same class as editing any save. Because the pair removes the remove-then-rename window, a missing-file state is reachable only by tampering, a first-ever write interrupted at creation, or media loss.
202	
203	**3.5 Reaching the sim.** `request_restore` and `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)` pass the epoch as an argument; the kernel range-checks it (`RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`, domain 0 code 6) and exposes it read-only, sim-visible and **non-persisted, non-hashed** in the `kernel.clock` read view as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` before the first `restore()`; it is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0003, TD-07). The one derivation, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch`, belongs to the kernel and ADR-0005 (`rng_derive_epoch`); Attention and Horror call it and never store the epoch (TR-attention-024, TR-horror-017). Determinism is defined given the pair: the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) replays identically, and tests pin the epoch. The phrase "excluded from the snapshot header" (TR-cmd-018) means *the kernel snapshot payload and every `H64`*: the **container** header carries the recovery copy of § 3.1, which is covered by the file trailer (file integrity) and by no state hash.
204	
205	**3.6 Staging and hot copy.** Candidate selection (SL-8), the death-stub's one synchronous attempt per candidate and the newest and preceding **hot decoded copies** (SL-11) stand as written; the hot copies are held by Save/Load and are never handed to a worker (a retained alias of a handed-over buffer is forbidden, § 1.6). The payload handed to `request_restore` is built in memory by Save/Load (not decoded from one blob): `Dictionary` of `StringName block_id -> {&"schema_version": int, &"data": Dictionary}`, with `kernel.clock` included, `data` dictionaries marked read-only as a shallow convenience (`Dictionary.make_read_only()` is **shallow**, probe 14, so owners copy what they keep, OQ-53; a deep read-only snapshot, where wanted, is built by the owner from `duplicate(true)` at capture). The expected hash is passed as **two typed arguments**: `expected_state_hash: int` (the header `state_hash`) and `has_expected_hash: bool`, `false` when the file legitimately carries none (a release-build file that predates K-4: verdict `NONE`). No `null` and no `Variant` (ADR-0002, TD-05; OQ-B closed): `Variant` is banned in typed interfaces, passing `null` to an `int` parameter is a runtime error, and a legitimate `H64` of 0 exists, so no value is a sentinel.
206	
207	### Key Interfaces

118	### 4. Ownership is a kernel binding table keyed by PlayerId
119	
120	Exactly as CR-7: half (a) `peer_id → PlayerId` is session state set by a host-only API (a boot step in the MVP: `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1), never touched by a restore, new game or death restart, and never resetting any issuer's `seq`. Half (b) `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}` is derived from saved state and is never saved; the kernel rebuilds it as the last step of every pass through `LOADING` from the registered binding sources in ascending `block_id` order. The data structure:
121	
122	- Half (a): a `Dictionary` `int → int`.
123	- Half (b): per PlayerId, one small `PlayerBindings` object holding two parallel `PackedInt64Array`s (source block index, entity id) behind one `add` / `remove` / `owns(source, entity)` interface, so the arrays cannot drift out of step. A player owns a handful of entities (an avatar and a beam), so `owns` is a linear scan of a few elements with no composite-key hashing and no allocation. Mutation is an explicit read-modify-write on the object's own arrays (never `dict[k].append(x)` on a packed array stored in a dictionary, whose behaviour has varied across versions), covered by a unit test.
124	- **Determinism of iteration.** The `LOADING` rebuild and every registry walk iterate **sorted** arrays (block ids ascending, command types in registration order recorded in an array), never `keys()` of a Dictionary filled from an unordered source. Dictionaries preserve insertion order in Godot 4, but erasing and re-inserting a key moves it to the end, so no hash or rebuild may depend on it.
125	
126	A command type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` passes P2 iff `(actor_source(type), actor)` is in half (b) of `PlayerId(issuer_peer)`; otherwise it is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` with no state change. Persistent state is keyed by PlayerId; the peer id appears only in the ingress stamp and the binding table. Ownership is **never** derived from scene-tree node ownership, `set_multiplayer_authority()` or any engine multiplayer primitive.
127	
128	### 5. Ordering, coalescing and the queue
129	
130	- Apply order is ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`, where `host_order` is the arrival counter at `_admit`; in single-player it is submission order (CR-13 G1).
131	- The queue is one preallocated ring of `Command` slots sized to `QUEUE_CAPACITY` with per-issuer counters for `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` and a `SYSTEM_RESERVE` so SYSTEM commands cannot be starved by a flood of PLAYER ones. Overflow is `QUEUE_FULL` at admission, never a silent drop. **Accounting rule:** the capacity counters (`QUEUE_CAPACITY`, `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY`) decrement the moment a command is superseded, P1 skips tombstones and counts only live commands against `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, and the tombstone's ring position is reclaimed when the head passes it, so an aim stream under backlog cannot cause a spurious `QUEUE_FULL`. On entry to `LOADING`, `SHUTTING_DOWN` or `FAULTED` the queue is flushed and every queued command receives `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` (the exactly-one-result guarantee, CR-5 and G5).
132	- **Coalescing** (`coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`) is done by scanning the unfrozen portion of the queue for a command with the same `(type_idx, actor, issuer_peer)` and marking the older one `Superseded`. The scan runs only when a coalescing type is submitted, and intent types are sent a few times per second (aim at most every 3 ticks), so the scan over at most 1,024 slots is cheap and avoids a second index structure that would have to be kept in step with the ring. A type with `coalesce ≠ NONE` that allows both origins fails boot (`COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`).
133	- Each tick, P1 moves at most `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` commands into the frozen batch for P2; the rest wait FIFO.
134	- A command older than its type's `max_age_ticks` is `STALE`. At local defaults this is unreachable (CR-17) and is guarded by an invariant test.
135	
136	### 6. The control plane is a host-local API on a `ControlHandle`
137	
138	`request_pause()`, `request_resume()`, `request_snapshot()`, `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`, `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch)`, `request_shutdown()`, `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are methods of `ControlHandle`, not commands. They are not stamped, queued, authority-checked or logged as commands. Each call is appended to a small host-local request list and served **at the next boundary service, in arrival order** (ADR-0001 § 1), and each request ends in exactly one outcome: `SERVED`, `DEFERRED` (made while an atomic step was active; evaluated at the first boundary after it) or `IGNORED` (a (state, trigger) pair the transition table does not list; one invalid-transition entry, no state change). **Outcome delivery.** Outcomes are always recorded in diagnostics. Callers that must act on one set `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler(Callable)` and receive a typed `ControlOutcome` (`request_kind`, `outcome`, `tick`, and for `request_restore` the K-4 verdict `{T, computed_hash, verdict}` with `verdict` one of `MATCH`, `MISMATCH` or `NONE`; for `request_snapshot` the captured payload, a deep copy, plus the hash data listed below) at the same per-frame flush point as command results, **in a separate list that is never part of the CR-5 command result buffer**. This amends one sentence of the kernel GDD (States and Transitions, "control-plane requests have none"; § GDD sync): the outcome list is not a command result record, but it exists, because Save/Load needs the snapshot payload and the K-4 verdict (CR-15) and PauseGate needs to converge. **Snapshot outcome carries the hash data (amended 2026-10-28, TD-05).** `request_snapshot()` stays asynchronous and returns `void`; its result arrives only through the outcome handler. The snapshot `ControlOutcome` adds `T: int`, `world_seed: int`, `state_hash: int`, `hash_algo: int`, `block_ids: Array[StringName]`, `schema_versions: PackedInt64Array`, `block_state_hashes: PackedInt64Array` and `enc_lens: PackedInt64Array`. The four arrays are parallel (index `i` describes `block_ids[i]`), sorted by `block_id`, and cover **every persist block, WORLD and PROFILE**; all hashes and lengths are computed uncached inside `SAVING` (ADR-0005 § 4.7 and § 5.4). ADR-0005 owns what the hash values mean; this ADR owns only that they travel on the outcome. **Restore verdict.** `request_restore(payload: Dictionary, restore_epoch: int, expected_state_hash: int = 0, has_expected_hash: bool = false)`: the "no verdict" case is a typed `bool`, not `Variant` or `null`, because ADR-0010 bans `Variant` in typed interfaces and `0` is a legal H64 (ADR-0005 reserves no sentinel value). When `has_expected_hash` is `false` the K-4 compare is skipped, `expected_state_hash` is ignored and the outcome's verdict is `NONE` (the pre-K-4 release file case). When it is `true` the verdict is `MATCH` or `MISMATCH`. A reproduction mismatch remains a diagnostic (CR-15); the verdict never changes the restore result.
139	
140	Two consequences are intentional: a `request_pause` and a `request_resume` in the same boundary pair up in order, and `PauseGate` (Chart Table) re-issues the latest desired pause state until the kernel matches it, so a same-boundary pair leaves no wedged half-open state (TR-charttable-004).
141	
142	**Seat binding (binding table half (a)).** `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are the host-only writers of `peer_id → PlayerId` (CR-7). The composition root, holding the `game` control handle, calls `request_bind_seat(HOST_PEER_ID, 1)` as its boot step; the Co-op Session calls the same two methods in VS-B, so the kernel's public API does not widen then. A restore, new game or death restart never touches half (a). Runtime seat reassignment (kernel open question 4) is deferred to ADR-0032 under this signature. 143	
144	Pause is single-player only. While `PAUSED` the kernel accepts only command types flagged `allowed_when_paused` whose `writes_blocks` name no `gameplay = true` block; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` at admission without queuing (CR-16). The control plane is host-local by construction: a remote ingress has no `ControlHandle`.
145	
146	This ADR owns how requests are accepted, ordered and answered. The states they move between (`RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`) and the transitions' internals belong to ADR-0003.
