gdd_sync.old: Restore order follows declared `restore_after`; a cycle in it, or a reference to an unregistered block, fails boot.
gdd_sync.new: Restore order follows declared `restore_after`, and `post_restore`, `default_state` and `init_world` follow the same order (ties: smallest registration index, as for hooks); a cycle (including a self edge), a reference to an unregistered block, or more than `MAX_BLOCKS` registered blocks fails boot (ADR-0016). A persisted block's `default_state(ctx)` ends with `ctx.put(payload)`, applied through the block's own `restore`. A `binding_source` delivers one flat ascending `PackedInt64Array` of (player_id, entity_id) pairs.

gdd_sync.old: a pre-check fails (`RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK`, `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)
gdd_sync.new: a pre-check fails (`RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK`, `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`, `RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`), run over the whole payload before any `restore()` with the blocks, the clock and binding half (b) intact

gdd_sync.old: Whether `post_restore` order follows `restore_after` is **informational only** (CR-8 and KRN:843 say "after every `restore()`"); no Layout rule depends on the answer.
gdd_sync.new: `post_restore` order follows the `restore_after` DAG (ADR-0016): Layout, the root, runs first, so every later block's `post_restore` sees Layout's leaf-dependent queries already derived. The version bump below stays as belt and braces; no Layout rule depends on the order.

gdd_sync.old: The kernel does not state that `post_restore` calls follow `restore_after`
gdd_sync.new: The kernel states (ADR-0016) that `post_restore` calls follow `restore_after`, so Layout's `derive_doors` pass has run before the Emitter's cold build; Open Question 26 is granted

gdd_sync.old: re-register all subjects idempotently (IA-37) before the first `emitter.place` (EM-21).
gdd_sync.new: `post_restore` writes only `interaction.state` and never the Emitter or the Controller (ADR-0016): it rebuilds the candidate table and window `W` and compares the Emitter's persisted registered subjects with `W`, recording `IA_RESTORE_SUBJECT_DRIFT` on a difference; the repair is the ordinary `interaction` hook rule, which runs before the first `emitter.place` after a load. The channel, door-attempt and `last_result` drops are an interim `REBASE_BLOCKS` normalisation whose exit is `snapshot()` writing the dropped form.

gdd_sync.old: until their owners move the clears into `snapshot()` the build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` (SL-12) names such blocks, and it must be empty at the first outside build
gdd_sync.new: until their owners move the clears into `snapshot()` the build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` (SL-12) names such blocks, as a committed array with one data row per member {block_id, owner_adr, reason, exit}; CI fails on a stale or missing entry and on a non-empty list in an outside-release build; every persisted block supplies a `FixtureFactory` (ADR-0016 section 9)

gdd_sync.old: never by clamping
gdd_sync.new: never by clamping, except the stock reconcile for a store above a lowered live `stock_cap`, which runs at the head of phase 0 of the first Graph step, credits `disc_*`, counts `stock_clamped` and emits the diagnostic; the restore itself stays byte-identical (ADR-0011 section 7.3, accepted by ADR-0016 section 4.4)

gdd_sync.old: **restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).
gdd_sync.new: **restore_after order (MVP, ADR-0016 section 2.4):** `layout.state`, `graph.state`, `body.state`, `suit.state`, `controller.state`, `emitter.state`, `interaction.state`, `assembly.state`, `web.state`, `attention.state`, `horror.state`, `sanity.state`, `sanity.ledger`, then the non-persisted `sanity.perception`; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG with smallest registration index first among ready blocks, and `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state` and `init_world` all follow it.

foundation_asks.ask: Append kernel fault codes after 17 MEMORY_BUDGET (never renumbered): 18 RESTORE_CYCLE (boot: cycle or self edge in restore_after), 19 BLOCK_LIMIT (boot: more than MAX_BLOCKS blocks registered), 20 RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (pre-check: stored schema_version not in supported_versions, before any restore()), 21 DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD (a persisted block's default_state returned without ctx.put); add boot warning RESTORE_AFTER_DUPLICATE.

State that BlockDescriptor.restore_after orders restore, post_restore, default_state and init_world; that the registry validation pass (section 8) compiles the RestorePlan (Kahn, smallest registration index first) as a new step after the hook schedule; that the RESTORE WriteScope phase for post_restore also opens the restoring block only (confirming section 4); and that a persisted block's default_state ends with ctx.put(payload) of snapshot shape which the kernel applies through that block's own restore.

Specify the binding_source payload as one flat PackedInt64Array of (player_id, entity_id) pairs, strictly ascending, and that the kernel validates its shape (even length, player_id >= 1, order) with BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT detail reasons CONFLICT_OWNER, DUPLICATE_TRIPLE, SHAPE, ORDER, PLAYER_RANGE, SOURCE_FAULT.

Extend the restore ControlOutcome with load_ok: bool, fail_stage: int, fail_block: StringName, fail_code: int, defaulted_blocks: Array[StringName] (so Save/Load can map an owner-failed load to RESTORE_FAILED and report REBASED cause 3). In section 4 state that the binding rebuild walks sources in ascending String(block_id), not StringName order (probed 2026-10-29: StringName < and sort() are not lexical), and that half (b) is cleared after the pre-check passes and left empty when a pass faults.

Fix the fields of the kernel.clock entry in the staged payload (T, world_seed, tick_rate) so the kernel pre-check TICK_RATE_MISMATCH can run; confirm REBASE_BLOCKS is a committed array with a data row per member and a CI gate (stale entry, missing entry, non-empty in an outside-release build) flipped by the same SHIPPED decision as the ADR-0007 ledgers; record that a failed owner restore falls to the next candidate by a new pass (the pre-restore world is not recoverable).

In section 5.2 add post_restore to the calls after which the kernel resets the hash-cache entry (serial = -1) for the block, alongside restore, init_world and default_state, so a REBASE_BLOCKS normalisation in post_restore can never leave a stale cached hash.

Add a lint pack RST: RST-01 (error, src/kernel, src/save, src/shared) no <, > or .sort() on StringName operands or Array[StringName] outside BlockIdOrder.less; RST-02 (error, src/sim) files named *_restore.gd or *_verify.gd reference no other block's mutator class; RST-03 (error, src/) init_world( is called only from src/kernel/; and a doc-tag check that every read-view method carries a Tier S or Tier D tag. Add src/shared/block_id_order.gd and src/shared/restore/verify_out.gd to the L0 layout table.

decisions.chosen: Same DAG order as restore (post_order is order filtered to WORLD persisted plus non-persisted blocks)
decisions.reason: Architecture Data Flow 7 already says it; Emitter OQ-26 and ADR-0019 depend on it; costs nothing; Layout's 'informational only' is compatible; keeps the Layout version-bump self-heal as belt and braces.

decisions.chosen: Smallest registration index among ready blocks, the same Kahn rule as the hook sort (ADR-0003 section 8); alternative linear extensions tested by KRN-RST-05
decisions.reason: One algorithm and one total order that is a pure function of registration data; advisor recommendation, adopted over an initial preference for String(block_id) ordering (kept only for the binding walk); probe P2 shows the tie-break changes the order so the permutation test guards it.

decisions.chosen: Ascending String(block_id) via BlockIdOrder.less; StringName ordering forbidden (lint RST-01)
decisions.reason: TR-cmd-013 says ascending block_id; probed 2026-10-29 that StringName < and sort() are not lexical on 4.7.2.

decisions.chosen: Distributed, owner-held pure functions called from the owner's restore/post_restore at its DAG slot; ADR-0016 owns the numbered list V1..V16 and the order; no kernel verifier registry
decisions.reason: Kernel H1 forbids domain rules in the kernel; matches the TR rows ('in post_restore'); no new registrar surface; the separate verification stage stays as the documented second move (Alternative 3).

decisions.chosen: One numbered sequence per pass; first fault stops the pass; FAULTED with no tick, no command, no snapshot, no ALL batch, load_seq unchanged, empty half (b); only request_restore/request_new_game exit; pre-restore state intact only for pre-check failures
decisions.reason: Answers ADR-0011's cross-ADR ask that a faulted LOADING never plays; matches the kernel GDD edge case; each exit replaces every WORLD block.

decisions.chosen: No automatic revert and no validate-all-first phase
decisions.reason: A revert is a second pass that can fail; no MVP caller has a live world worth keeping (Continue from title, death stub); cross-block checks like Body liveness need Layout already committed.

decisions.chosen: Persisted block's default_state ends with ctx.put(payload); the kernel applies it through the block's own restore; no put is DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD; non-persisted blocks reset derived members
decisions.reason: One copy path validates every default on every new game and absent-block restore; consistent with the GDD's 'default_state ... ctx.put(state)'.

decisions.point: Absent persisted block on restore and non-persisted blocks
decisions.chosen: Absent WORLD block gets default_state at its DAG slot; non-persisted blocks get default_state then post_restore in DAG position; PROFILE blocks are skipped by in-session passes
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 2.2 (REBASED cause 3 is Save/Load's to report); in-session restore never rolls back PROFILE (Pillar 5).

decisions.chosen: Derived members only; no persisted-column write except a REBASE_BLOCKS member's normalisation; no cross-block write; no clamp/prune/repair; submit impossible
decisions.reason: Keeps hash-after-post_restore equal to hash-after-restore, K-4 at MATCH, and TR-sanity-019; the RESTORE scope already forbids cross-block writes.

decisions.chosen: Always an ordinary hook rule that is a no-op on consistent state; no first-run-after-restore branch
decisions.reason: Kernel G4 requires equal state_hash at every tick between restored and uninterrupted runs; KRN-RST-11 checks it.

decisions.chosen: Keep ADR-0003 RESTORE scope (restoring block only); Interaction detects drift in post_restore and repairs in its hook before emitter.place; widening the scope is Alternative 6
decisions.reason: Emitter subject registrations and lit bits are persisted (TR-emitter-007) so re-registration is redundant for a consistent save; avoids a hash-visible cross-block write at load.

decisions.point: Stock reconcile for a lowered stock_cap (TR-itemdb-033)
decisions.chosen: Accept ADR-0011: restore byte-identical, reconcile at the head of Graph phase 0, not in post_restore
decisions.reason: Keeps K-4 MATCH, no REBASED cause owed to ADR-0006, and post_restore stays derived-only.

decisions.chosen: Tier S (persisted-answerable) vs Tier D (needs owner post_restore); post_restore reads Tier D only of DAG predecessors; restore reads Tier S of closure predecessors only
decisions.reason: Generalises Layout's class 1/class 2 split (TR-section-008) into a rule the permutation test can falsify.

decisions.chosen: Normalise in snapshot(); FixtureFactory per persisted block; harness enumerates the registry; REBASE_BLOCKS is a data-backed list with a CI gate; interim member interaction.state
decisions.reason: SL-12/SL-15 item 10 and TR-saveload-034; Assembly and Controller already normalise in snapshot(); makes the first-outside-build exit checkable.

decisions.chosen: Whole-payload pre-check after flush and before any clock install or restore(); add kernel code RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED; half (b) cleared only after the pre-check passes
decisions.reason: TR-cmd-036 requires state intact; without a kernel version code only an owner could fault a mismatch, after the swap.

decisions.chosen: RESTORE_CYCLE, BLOCK_LIMIT, RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD as ADR-0003 asks; duplicate restore_after entries are a boot warning
decisions.reason: TR-cmd-035 needs a cycle code distinct from HOOK_CYCLE and a MAX_BLOCKS code; self edge is a cycle.

decisions.chosen: SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH stays in Suit's post_restore (SE-13); a one-holder check (carry_ref below Interaction's counter and not in loose[]) is proposed as V11 for ADR-0020
decisions.reason: ADR-0019 hands 'whether carry_ref resolves' to this ADR; Interaction's reason list is closed so the owner must accept it.

decisions.chosen: KRN-RST-10 asserts OBJECT_COUNT, OBJECT_NODE_COUNT and OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT stable across 100 restore/new-game alternations; render-texture and pool legs left to ADR-0028
decisions.reason: Probes P3 and P4 show the monitors work headless and detect a retained cycle; render-texture count API is UNVERIFIED.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Answers the Layout and others read before the Graph's post_restore come from persisted columns only (Tier S): RoomSource, step_no (from hdr), opening_into, seam_openings_into, section_counts_into; Graph restore_after is [layout.state]; the stock reconcile for a lowered stock_cap runs at the head of phase 0 (Open Question 2 closed this way) and ADR-0012 implements it; Graph default_state builds a snapshot-shaped payload that its own restore accepts.

layout.state restore_after is [] (the DAG root); its class 1 queries are Tier S and class 2 are Tier D with the stale_leaf diagnostic; post_restore runs derive_doors then the cross-block checks (graph_ref_base, weld seam_ids, next_section_id equality) reading only Graph Tier S; any geometry-hash rewrite stays a restore() case accepted as a REBASED cause, not a standing REBASE_BLOCKS member; default_state builds a payload its restore accepts.

controller.state restore_after is [body.state, suit.state] and neither Body nor Suit declares an edge on the Controller (verified from the GDDs); the Controller's post_restore reads Suit's cap after Suit's own post_restore, which the shared DAG order guarantees; the Controller normalises transient fields in snapshot() (PC-17); the carry_ref cross-check is Suit's (SE-13) plus the proposed V11.

body.state restore_after is [layout.state]; its restore reads Layout Tier S only; seat_bindings() is a pure read from SEAT rows registered as BlockDescriptor.binding_source; post_restore only sets pos_prev := pos_curr and world_prev := world, counts the trapped-actor probe and never faults on overlap; Body never rebuilds the kernel binding.

Propagation phase 0 contains the stock reconcile as an idempotent steady-state rule (no first-run flag) and the seeds written by Graph post_restore make the first run reproduce an uninterrupted run (KRN-RST-11).

emitter.state restore_after is [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]; its post_restore rebuilds all derived state in ascending id including the static layer and keeps each subject's lit bit; beam_bindings() is a pure read registered as emitter.state's binding_source; the Emitter exposes persisted subject registrations (Tier S) so Interaction can compare them with W; emitter.place is ordered after the Interaction hook that repairs subject drift.

interaction.state post_restore writes only interaction.state; it detects Emitter subject drift and the hook repairs it before emitter.place; the channel, door-attempt and last_result clears are an interim REBASE_BLOCKS normalisation with an exit that moves them into snapshot(); verifier V11 (carry_ref below the instance counter and not in loose[]) is accepted into the closed reason list or dropped.

Owns the INV-1..INV-7 and INV-10 bodies and the apply-time call sites; the release subset after weld/cut is INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-7 using the same verify function with a subset mask; assembly.state restore_after is [layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state] and snapshot() writes pending as NONE.

attention.state restore_after is [graph.state, emitter.state]; post_restore rebuilds caches only; the beacon is reconciled by an idempotent rule in the first attention.step; locus ids resolve against Graph and Emitter Tier S.
